The test image shows a tomato leaf with tan/brown necrotic lesions covered by a dense, fluffy grayish-brown fuzzy growth. This strongly suggests **Gray Mold** (Botrytis). The gray-brown velvety sporulation is very characteristic.

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image confirms Gray Mold: tan-to-brown necrotic lesions on tomato leaves, similar shape and coloration to the test image. The test image additionally shows the hallmark dense fuzzy gray-brown sporulation (the powdery/fluffy texture on the lesions), which is the defining characteristic of Botrytis (Gray Mold).

Key matching features:
- Tan/brown necrotic lesions on a green tomato leaf
- Dense, fluffy/velvety gray-brown spore mass on the necrotic tissue
- Irregular lesion shape consistent with Botrytis infection
- No concentric rings (rules out Early Blight), no small specks (rules out Bacterial Speck), no white powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)
